ask: snake on a 10 x 10 board, pixels on a canvas, a grid widget or a canvas the board fills: a button labelled Start begins, and shows only while no game runs; the snake starts 5 squares long on row 4 (rows and columns from 0), on columns 1 to 5, its head at column 5, moving right one square every 200 ms; the arrow keys turn it at its next step, never straight back; past an edge it comes back on the other side; it is green (2) and the one food red (1), on a random free square; eating the food makes it one longer and puts new food down; running into itself ends the game: it stops and says Game over; a label shows Length: N
check:
# Snake that wraps, on a 10 x 10 board: the body green (2), the one food red (1); it starts 5
# long on row 4, columns 1 to 5, moving right a square every 200 ms.
click "Start"
expect squares 2 10x10 = 5
expect squares 1 10x10 = 1
expect color 1 4 10x10 = 2
expect color 3 4 10x10 = 2
expect color 5 4 10x10 = 2
expect after "length" = 5
expect not has "Start"
wait 200
expect color 6 4 10x10 = 2      # a step right
wait 1400
expect color 3 4 10x10 = 2      # 7 steps on, past the right edge: column 3
expect not says "game over"
key "down"
wait 200
expect color 3 5 10x10 = 2      # turned down
key "up"
wait 200
expect color 3 6 10x10 = 2      # never straight back
key "right"
wait 200
expect color 4 6 10x10 = 2
key "up"
wait 200
expect color 4 5 10x10 = 2
expect not says "game over"
key "left"
wait 200
expect says "game over"         # it ran into itself
expect has "Start"
mark
wait 1000
expect same                     # nothing moves once it is over
click "Start"
expect not says "game over"
expect squares 2 10x10 = 5
expect color 1 4 10x10 = 2
expect after "length" = 5

ask: a memory game: 16 cards face down on a 4 x 4 board, a grid widget or a canvas the board fills, hiding 8 pairs; the first game's pairs lie side by side, row by row (squares 0 and 1 a pair, 2 and 3, and so on), and a button labelled New game deals them again, shuffled at random; a face-down card is gray (8); a tap turns a card face up, showing its color (never gray) or symbol; tapping a card already face up does nothing; two face-up cards that match stay up, two that do not turn face down again at the next tap or after a second; it counts moves (each two cards turned is one) as Moves: N and says You win when every pair is found
check:
# Memory on a 4 x 4 board: face down gray (8), face up never gray; the first game in pairs side
# by side, row by row (squares 0 and 1 a pair, 2 and 3, ...).
expect after "moves" = 0
expect squares 8 4x4 = 16
expect not says "you win"
tapcell 0 0 4x4
expect squares 8 4x4 = 15
expect color 0 0 4x4 != 8
tapcell 0 0 4x4                 # a card face up, tapped again: nothing
expect squares 8 4x4 = 15
expect after "moves" = 0
tapcell 2 0 4x4                 # not its pair
expect after "moves" = 1
expect squares 8 4x4 = 14
wait 1500
tapcell 0 1 4x4                 # the two turned down (then, or a second after)
expect squares 8 4x4 = 15
expect color 0 0 4x4 = 8
expect color 2 0 4x4 = 8
tapcell 1 1 4x4                 # a pair stays up
expect after "moves" = 2
expect squares 8 4x4 = 14
wait 1500
tapcell 0 0 4x4
expect squares 8 4x4 = 13
tapcell 1 0 4x4
expect squares 8 4x4 = 12
wait 1500
tapcell 2 0 4x4
tapcell 3 0 4x4
tapcell 2 1 4x4
tapcell 3 1 4x4
tapcell 0 2 4x4
tapcell 1 2 4x4
tapcell 2 2 4x4
tapcell 3 2 4x4
tapcell 0 3 4x4
tapcell 1 3 4x4
tapcell 2 3 4x4
expect not says "you win"
expect squares 8 4x4 = 1
tapcell 3 3 4x4
expect squares 8 4x4 = 0
expect says "you win"
expect after "moves" = 9
click "New game"
expect squares 8 4x4 = 16
expect after "moves" = 0
expect not says "you win"
tapcell 0 0 4x4                 # one card up, then a new game: it starts afresh
click "New game"
expect squares 8 4x4 = 16
tapcell 1 0 4x4
tapcell 2 0 4x4
expect after "moves" = 1
expect squares 8 4x4 = 14

ask: 2048 on a 4 x 4 board on a canvas: each tile a square with its number written on it as text, the empty squares gray (8) and no tile gray; every game, the first and each one a button labelled New game starts, begins with a 2 in the top left square and a 2 in the top right square; the arrow keys and buttons labelled Up, Down, Left and Right slide the tiles as far as they go; two equal tiles that meet merge into one of their sum, which adds to the score; after each move that changes the board a 2 or a 4 appears on a random empty square, and after one that changes nothing none does; it shows the score as Score N in a label above the canvas and no other numbers, and says Game over when no move is left

expect color 3 0 4x4 != 8
expect after "score" = 0
expect not number > 2
mark
key "up"                        # nothing moves: no new tile
expect same

expect after "score" = 4
expect color 0 0 4x4 != 8
expect squares 8 4x4 = 14       # the 4 and a new tile
expect number = 4
click "New game"
expect squares 8 4x4 = 14
expect after "score" = 0
expect not number > 2
click "Right"
expect after "score" = 4
expect color 3 0 4x4 != 8
expect squares 8 4x4 = 14
click "New game"
key "down"                      # both fall to the bottom row, apart
expect after "score" = 0
expect color 0 3 4x4 != 8
expect color 3 3 4x4 != 8
expect squares 8 4x4 = 13
click "New game"
mark
click "Up"
expect same
click "Left"
expect after "score" = 4
click "New game"
key "right"
expect after "score" = 4
click "New game"
click "Down"
expect squares 8 4x4 = 13
expect after "score" = 0
repeat 4: key "left"
repeat 4: click "Down"
key "right"
click "Up"
key "left"
key "down"
click "Right"
key "down"
click "Left"
key "down"
key "right"
key "up"
click "Left"
key "down"
expect not number = 3           # tiles are 2, 4, 8 ...; the score is a sum of merges
expect not number = 5
expect not number = 6
expect not number = 7
click "New game"
expect squares 8 4x4 = 14
expect after "score" = 0
expect not number > 2

The lander is one yellow (3) square: on row 8 at heights 0 to 9, one row higher for every 10 more (row 0 at heights 80 to 89), and not shown above that. Labels show Height: N, Speed: N, Drift: N, Fuel: N, Round: N and Score: N. A button labelled Start begins a game of 3 rounds with fuel 30 and a score of 0, and shows only while no game runs; the fuel is not refilled between rounds. Each round begins with the lander at height 80 in column 1, at speed 0 (how fast it falls; below 0 it rises) and drift 0 (the columns it moves a step: -1 left, 1 right). Every 200 ms is a step: the speed grows by 1, the height drops by the speed, and the lander moves by its drift, never past column 0 or 11 (at an edge it stays, its drift unchanged). Up or space (or a button labelled Burn) burns: if any fuel is left, the speed drops by 3 at once and the fuel by 1. Left and right (or buttons labelled Left and Right) fire the side jets: if any fuel is left and the drift is not already -1 (for left) or 1 (for right), the drift changes by 1 that way at once and the fuel drops by 1. When the height reaches 0 or less the lander is down: over the pad, at a speed of 3 or less and a drift of 0, it has landed and the score goes up 100; otherwise it has crashed. A lander at a height under 10 over the hill (columns 4 to 6) crashes into it. Either way the next round begins at once; after the third the game stops and says Game over.

# A 4 x 4 pipes level; each piece is turned a half turn (two taps) or, if straight, once, so
# either way round reaches the same pipes. The water starts in the top left piece.
start
expect not says "you win|well done|congrat|you did it|solved!|puzzle solved|all connected|complete!"
repeat 2: tapcell 1 0 4x4
repeat 2: tapcell 0 1 4x4
repeat 2: tapcell 1 2 4x4
expect not says "you win|well done|congrat|you did it|solved!|puzzle solved|all connected|complete!"
tapcell 1 3 4x4
tapcell 2 3 4x4
repeat 2: tapcell 3 3 4x4
tapcell 3 2 4x4
expect not says "you win|well done|congrat|you did it|solved!|puzzle solved|all connected|complete!"
repeat 2: tapcell 2 1 4x4
repeat 2: tapcell 2 0 4x4
expect not says "you win|well done|congrat|you did it|solved!|puzzle solved|all connected|complete!"
repeat 2: tapcell 3 0 4x4
# All but the piece at 2, 2, which opens toward only some of the pipes that open toward it:
# water that ran through an opening on one side alone would reach every piece by now.
expect not says "you win|well done|congrat|you did it|solved!|puzzle solved|all connected|complete!"
repeat 2: tapcell 2 2 4x4       # the last piece: every pipe has water
expect says "solved|win|well done|congrat|complete|done|did it|connected|bravo|great"

A button labelled New game deals: you get the first 5 cards, the computer the next 5, the next card starts the pile and the rest make the stock, in that order. Everything is drawn on a canvas cut into 8 columns and 3 rows of equal cells: the computer's cards face down along the top row; the pile's top card in row 2, column 4, and the stock (face down while it holds cards) in row 2, column 5; your cards face up along the bottom row from the left, in the order you got them, closing up when one is played. A face-up card shows its name, like 10H or QS; no face-down card's name shows. You go first. A tap on one of your cards plays it onto the pile if it is an 8, or is of the suit to follow, or has the rank of the pile's top card; otherwise nothing happens. The suit to follow is the top card's suit, or the suit named for an 8: when you play an 8, buttons labelled Spades, Hearts, Diamonds and Clubs show, one to name the suit, and your cards do nothing until you choose. A tap on the stock adds its top card to the end of your hand and it is still your turn; when the stock is empty, a tap on it passes your turn. After each card you play (and the suit you name), the computer plays at once: the first card in its hand, in the order it got them, that it may play, an 8 only if nothing else fits; if nothing fits it draws from the stock one card at a time until one fits and plays that one, or passes when the stock runs out. When the computer plays an 8 it names the suit it then holds most of (ties go to spades, then hearts, diamonds, clubs). Labels show Computer: N cards, Stock: N, and Suit: and the suit to follow in full, like Suit: Hearts. When you have no cards left it says You win, when the computer has none it says Computer wins, and then taps do nothing until New game, which deals again from the same order.

On my turn I tap one of my hands that is not out to pick it, and it shows as picked (tapping my other hand picks that one instead), then tap one of the computer's hands that is not out: it gains my picked hand's fingers, and then nothing is picked. Tapping a hand that is out does nothing, and so does tapping the computer's hands with nothing picked. Then the computer answers at once: its hand with the most fingers (its left on a tie) adds them to my hand with the most fingers (my left on a tie). Labels show My left: N, My right: N, Its left: N and Its right: N. When the computer has no hand left it says You win; when I have none it says You lose; then the game is over, taps do nothing and Start shows again.
check:
# Me (the bottom row) against the computer (the top row) on a 2 x 2 board; it answers each move
# with its fullest hand on my fullest (left on a tie). 5 fingers or more puts a hand out.
expect has "Start"
click "Start"
expect not has "Start"
expect after "my left:" = 1
expect after "my right:" = 1
expect after "its left:" = 1
expect after "its right:" = 1
tapcell 0 0 2x2                 # nothing picked yet: nothing
expect after "its left:" = 1
expect after "my left:" = 1
mark
tapcell 0 1 2x2                 # my left, shown picked
expect changed
tapcell 0 0 2x2                 # onto its left: 2; it answers with that 2 on my left: 3
expect after "its left:" = 2
expect after "my left:" = 3
expect after "my right:" = 1
expect after "its right:" = 1
tapcell 0 1 2x2
tapcell 0 0 2x2                 # 3 onto 2: its left is out; its right hits my left: 4
expect after "its left:" = 0
expect after "my left:" = 4
expect after "its right:" = 1
expect after "my right:" = 1
tapcell 0 1 2x2
tapcell 0 0 2x2                 # its left is out: nothing, and my left stays picked
expect after "my left:" = 4
expect after "its right:" = 1
expect not says "you win"
tapcell 1 0 2x2                 # 4 onto 1: out, and the computer has no hand left
expect after "its right:" = 0
expect says "you win"
expect not says "you lose"
expect after "my left:" = 4     # no answer came
expect has "Start"
tapcell 1 1 2x2                 # over: taps do nothing
tapcell 1 0 2x2
expect after "my right:" = 1
expect after "its right:" = 0
click "Start"                   # a game I lose
expect after "my left:" = 1
expect after "its left:" = 1
expect after "its right:" = 1
expect not says "you win"
tapcell 0 1 2x2                 # my left, then my right instead
mark
tapcell 1 1 2x2
expect changed
tapcell 1 0 2x2                 # 1 onto its right: 2; its right (2) answers on my left (a tie): 3
expect after "its right:" = 2
expect after "its left:" = 1
expect after "my left:" = 3
expect after "my right:" = 1
tapcell 1 1 2x2
tapcell 0 0 2x2                 # its left 2; its left (a tie) puts my left out
expect after "its left:" = 2
expect after "my left:" = 0
expect after "my right:" = 1
tapcell 0 1 2x2                 # my left is out: nothing to pick
tapcell 0 0 2x2
expect after "its left:" = 2
tapcell 1 1 2x2
tapcell 0 0 2x2                 # its left 3; it hits my right: 4
expect after "its left:" = 3
expect after "my right:" = 4
expect not says "you lose"
tapcell 1 1 2x2
tapcell 1 0 2x2                 # 4 onto 2 puts its right out; its 3 puts my right out
expect after "its right:" = 0
expect after "my right:" = 0
expect after "its left:" = 3
expect says "you lose"
expect not says "you win"
expect has "Start"

ask: Black Box: 4 atoms hidden in an 8 x 8 box, on a canvas the board fills, cut into 10 x 10 equal squares (or a grid widget 10 wide): the box is columns 1 to 8 of rows 1 to 8 (counting from 0 at the top left), the rim is the squares around it (row 0 and row 9, column 0 and column 9, without the four corners). The atoms are at column 2 row 1, column 4 row 4, column 6 row 4 and column 6 row 7, shown only after Check. Rim squares are gray (8) until used, the box and the corners blank (0). A tap on a gray rim square sends a ray straight into the box from it. Step by step: if the square ahead holds an atom, the ray is absorbed (a hit); else, if an atom is on one side of the square ahead (diagonally in front), the ray turns 90 degrees away from it where it is, and if atoms are on both sides it turns back; if neither, it moves ahead. A ray that would turn while still on its rim square comes straight back. When the ray reaches the rim it leaves there. A hit marks the rim square red (1); a ray that leaves where it came in marks it yellow (3); a ray leaving elsewhere marks both its rim squares green (2). Used rim squares and corners do nothing when tapped. A tap on a box square puts a guess there (blue, 4) or takes it away. A label shows Score: N, one for each marked rim square, and Guesses: N. A button labelled Check shows the atoms: a guessed atom green (2), a wrong guess red (1), an atom not guessed purple (5); it adds 5 to the score for each atom not guessed, says Found N of 4, and taps then do nothing. A button labelled New game starts again with the same atoms.

expect after "score" = 6

expect color 0 3 10x10 = 2
expect color 9 2 10x10 = 2

ask: Fanorona for two on one screen: a board of 9 x 5 points on a canvas cut into 9 x 5 equal squares, a point in the middle of each (or a grid widget 9 wide), columns 0 to 8 from the left and rows 0 to 4 from the top. Lines join each point to its neighbours across and down, and diagonally too where the point's column and row add up to an even number. Blue (4) fills rows 0 and 1, red (1) rows 3 and 4; row 2 holds, from the left, blue, red, blue, red, empty, blue, red, blue, red. An empty point is gray (8) at its middle. Red moves first. A tap on one of your pieces picks it; a tap on an empty point next to it along a line moves it there. Moving toward an enemy piece that is then just beyond, along the same line, captures it and every enemy piece right behind it in that line (approach); moving straight away from an enemy piece just behind takes it and the enemy pieces in a row behind it (withdrawal); if a move could do both, it takes by approach. While any capture is possible, a move that captures nothing is not allowed (nothing happens). After a capture, the same piece must go on capturing while it can, but never moving the same way as its last move and never onto a point it has been on this turn; meanwhile other pieces can't move. Then the turn passes. A label shows Turn: Red or Turn: Blue, and another Red: N Blue: N, the pieces left. Taking all the other's pieces wins: it says Red wins or Blue wins.

ask: the 24 game: four cards on a 4 x 1 board, a grid widget or a canvas the board fills, each a blue (4) square showing its number. The puzzles come in this order, the cards from left to right: 4 7 8 8, then 1 2 3 4, then 3 4 5 6, then 2 2 6 6, then 2 4 5 7, then the first again. Tapping a card picks it (it turns yellow, 3; until an operator is pressed, tapping another card picks that one instead); then a button labelled +, -, * or / picks the operation, and tapping a second card combines the two: the second card's square shows first card op second card (a minus may go below 0) and the first card's square empties (no color, no number). ask: Untangle on a 6 x 6 board of squares drawn on a canvas the board fills (or 36 equal squares): six dots sit in squares, joined by straight lines between the squares' centers. Columns and rows count from 0 at the top left. At the start the dots are A at column 3 row 2, B at 4,0, C at 5,2, D at 3,5, E at 5,1 and F at 1,1, and the lines join A-B, B-C, C-D, D-E, E-F, F-A, A-C, A-D and D-F. A tap on a dot picks it; then a tap on an empty square moves the picked dot there (a tap on another dot picks that one instead; a tap on an empty square with nothing picked does nothing). A label shows Crossings: N, the pairs of lines that cross (two lines that share a dot never count), and Moves: N, the dots moved so far. When no lines cross it says Solved and taps change nothing more. A button labelled New puzzle puts every dot back where it started and Moves back to 0.
check:
# Untangle on 6 x 6: dots A (3,2) B (4,0) C (5,2) D (3,5) E (5,1) F (1,1); lines A-B B-C C-D D-E E-F F-A
# A-C A-D D-F. No dot ever lies on a line it is not on, so every way of counting crossings agrees.
start
expect after "crossings" = 4
expect after "moves" = 0
expect not says "solved"
tapcell 2 4 6x6          # nothing picked: nothing
expect after "crossings" = 4
expect after "moves" = 0
tapcell 5 1 6x6          # E
tapcell 1 1 6x6          # F instead
tapcell 2 3 6x6          # F moves
expect after "crossings" = 5
expect after "moves" = 1
tapcell 2 3 6x6
tapcell 1 1 6x6          # and back
expect after "crossings" = 4
expect after "moves" = 2
tapcell 3 2 6x6          # A
tapcell 4 0 6x6          # B instead
tapcell 4 4 6x6          # B moves
expect after "crossings" = 3
expect after "moves" = 3
tapcell 4 4 6x6
tapcell 4 0 6x6          # and back
expect after "crossings" = 4
expect after "moves" = 4
tapcell 3 2 6x6          # A
tapcell 1 0 6x6
expect after "crossings" = 5
expect after "moves" = 5
expect not says "solved"
tapcell 1 1 6x6          # F
tapcell 0 2 6x6
expect after "crossings" = 5
expect after "moves" = 6
expect not says "solved"
tapcell 5 1 6x6          # E
tapcell 0 4 6x6
expect after "crossings" = 0
expect after "moves" = 7
expect says "solved"
mark
tapcell 0 4 6x6
tapcell 2 2 6x6          # solved: taps change nothing
expect same
click "New puzzle"
expect after "crossings" = 4
expect after "moves" = 0
expect not says "solved"
tapcell 1 1 6x6
tapcell 2 1 6x6
expect after "crossings" = 4
expect after "moves" = 1
tapcell 3 2 6x6          # A, where it started
tapcell 1 0 6x6
expect after "crossings" = 4
expect after "moves" = 2

ask: Jungle chess (Dou Shou Qi) for two players on one screen, on a 7 x 9 board drawn on a canvas the board fills (or 63 equal squares). Columns and rows count from 0 at the top left. The animals by rank: rat 1, cat 2, dog 3, wolf 4, leopard 5, tiger 6, lion 7, elephant 8; each shows its side's color at its square's middle, red (1) or blue (4), with its rank. Blue starts with the lion at column 0 row 0, tiger 6,0, dog 1,1, cat 5,1, rat 0,2, leopard 2,2, wolf 4,2 and elephant 6,2; red starts mirrored (its animal at column c row r where blue's is at 6-c, 8-r: lion 6,8, tiger 0,8, dog 5,7, cat 1,7, rat 6,6, leopard 4,6, wolf 2,6, elephant 0,6). Water fills columns 1, 2, 4 and 5 of rows 3 to 5 and shows cyan (6); blue's den is at 3,0 and red's at 3,8, each with three traps beside it (2,0, 4,0 and 3,1; 2,8, 4,8 and 3,7). Other taps do nothing. A label says Red to move or Blue to move. Moving into the enemy's den, or taking its last animal, wins: it says Red wins or Blue wins, and taps change nothing more. # Hasami shogi for two on 9 x 9, red (1) on the top row, blue (4) on the bottom, red first: a tap picks a
# piece, a tap on an empty square along its row or column with nothing between moves it. Pieces of the
# other side lying between the moved piece and another of the mover's are taken; moving in between is
# safe. Taking 3 wins.
start
expect squares 1 9x9 = 9
expect squares 4 9x9 = 9
expect says "red's turn"
tapcell 3 0 9x9
tapcell 3 4 9x9
expect color 3 4 9x9 = 1
expect color 3 0 9x9 = 0
expect says "blue's turn"
tapcell 4 0 9x9              # red's piece on blue's turn: nothing
tapcell 4 1 9x9
expect color 4 0 9x9 = 1
expect color 4 1 9x9 = 0
tapcell 0 8 9x9
tapcell 0 5 9x9
expect color 0 5 9x9 = 4
tapcell 0 0 9x9
tapcell 0 6 9x9              # blue at 0,5 is in the way: nothing
expect color 0 6 9x9 = 0
tapcell 3 4 9x9
tapcell 4 5 9x9              # not along a row or column: nothing
expect color 4 5 9x9 = 0
expect says "red's turn"
tapcell 2 0 9x9
tapcell 2 6 9x9
tapcell 8 8 9x9
tapcell 8 7 9x9
tapcell 2 6 9x9
tapcell 3 6 9x9
tapcell 0 5 9x9
tapcell 3 5 9x9              # between red 3,4 and 3,6: safe
expect color 3 5 9x9 = 4
expect squares 1 9x9 = 9
expect squares 4 9x9 = 9
tapcell 4 0 9x9
tapcell 4 5 9x9
expect color 3 5 9x9 = 4
tapcell 8 7 9x9
tapcell 8 6 9x9
tapcell 1 0 9x9
tapcell 1 5 9x9
tapcell 8 6 9x9
tapcell 8 7 9x9
tapcell 1 5 9x9
tapcell 2 5 9x9              # blue 3,5 between red 2,5 and 4,5: taken
expect color 3 5 9x9 = 0
expect squares 4 9x9 = 8
expect squares 1 9x9 = 9
tapcell 2 8 9x9
tapcell 2 6 9x9
tapcell 0 0 9x9
tapcell 0 1 9x9
tapcell 4 8 9x9
tapcell 4 6 9x9              # red 3,6 between blue 2,6 and 4,6: taken
expect color 3 6 9x9 = 0
expect squares 1 9x9 = 8
expect squares 4 9x9 = 8
tapcell 0 1 9x9
tapcell 0 2 9x9
tapcell 5 8 9x9
tapcell 5 5 9x9
tapcell 0 2 9x9
tapcell 0 3 9x9
tapcell 6 8 9x9
tapcell 6 5 9x9
expect not says "red wins|blue wins"
tapcell 7 0 9x9
tapcell 7 5 9x9              # blue 5,5 and 6,5 between red 4,5 and 7,5: both taken, red has 3
expect color 5 5 9x9 = 0
expect color 6 5 9x9 = 0
expect squares 4 9x9 = 6
expect squares 1 9x9 = 8
expect says "red wins"
expect not says "blue wins"
mark
tapcell 1 8 9x9
tapcell 1 6 9x9
expect same
tapcell 7 5 9x9
tapcell 7 6 9x9              # nor red's
expect same

# (0) on the bottom, each the color of its square. Each moves the tower of the color the other last landed
# on, straight or diagonally ahead; a tower with no move passes. Reaching the far row wins.

expect color 0 0 5x5 = 9
expect color 4 4 5x5 = 0
expect color 2 2 5x5 = 2
expect color 1 1 5x5 = 4

tapcell 3 3 5x5

expect color 3 3 5x5 = 5
tapcell 3 0 5x5
tapcell 0 3 5x5              # blue, diagonally to a green square
expect color 0 3 5x5 = 9
expect color 3 0 5x5 = 4
expect says "white's turn"
tapcell 2 4 5x5              # not the green tower: nothing
tapcell 2 3 5x5
expect color 2 4 5x5 = 0
expect color 2 3 5x5 = 4
tapcell 3 4 5x5
tapcell 3 2 5x5              # green, to a yellow square
expect color 3 2 5x5 = 0
expect color 3 4 5x5 = 2
tapcell 2 0 5x5
tapcell 3 0 5x5              # sideways: nothing
expect color 3 0 5x5 = 4
tapcell 2 0 5x5
tapcell 2 1 5x5              # yellow, to a purple square
expect color 2 1 5x5 = 9
tapcell 1 4 5x5
tapcell 1 3 5x5              # purple, to a yellow square
expect color 1 3 5x5 = 0
tapcell 2 1 5x5
tapcell 2 0 5x5              # back: nothing
tapcell 2 1 5x5
tapcell 0 3 5x5              # a tower on it: nothing
expect color 2 0 5x5 = 3
expect not says "black wins|white wins"
tapcell 2 1 5x5
tapcell 4 3 5x5              # over white's tower at 3,2: nothing
expect color 4 3 5x5 = 1
expect color 2 1 5x5 = 9
tapcell 2 1 5x5
tapcell 2 1 5x5              # tapped again: still picked

expect color 0 4 5x5 = 0

tapcell 1 4 5x5              # black's blue tower (the color under white's stuck one) reaches the bottom row

expect not says "white wins"
